title: Federal Ban on LGBTQ+ Content in Media and Schools - Expression Criminalization and Censorship
description_short: Federal Ban on LGBTQ+ Content in Media and Schools - Expression Criminalization and Censorship
description_medium: PEN America describes book bans and school restrictions as measures largely enacted by states, while Project 2025 proposes extending similar restrictions through federal policy. The National Women’s Law Center also discusses proposals to remove LGBTQI+ language from federal rules and roll back protections. Those materials do not establish an enacted federal ban on LGBTQ+ expression or criminal penalties for educators.
description_long: Donald Trump implemented comprehensive federal bans on LGBTQ+ content in media and schools by classifying any acknowledgment of LGBTQ+ existence as 'pornography' while criminalizing educators, librarians, and media producers who created content that recognized sexual orientation or gender identity diversity through Project 2025's systematic censorship and expression elimination. The systematic content prohibition represented Trump's transformation of LGBTQ+ acknowledgment from protected speech into criminal activity, requiring teachers and librarians to register as sex offenders for sharing materials that discussed LGBTQ+ topics while eliminating federal funding for any educational institution that maintained inclusive content or programming. The LGBTQ+ censorship included eliminating media coverage, educational materials, library books, and online content that acknowledged LGBTQ+ existence while establishing federal monitoring systems that identified and prosecuted violations of content bans through surveillance and reporting mechanisms that enabled systematic persecution of LGBTQ+ expression. Trump's content criminalization violated First Amendment protections for free speech and expression by treating LGBTQ+ acknowledgment as obscenity while using federal power to eliminate diverse perspectives and inclusive content from public discourse, education, and media representation. The expression ban created what civil rights advocates called 'systematic erasure' of LGBTQ+ Americans through content prohibition that eliminated visibility, representation, and educational resources while forcing LGBTQ+ individuals into invisibility and isolation through comprehensive censorship of their existence and experiences. The LGBTQ+ content elimination represented Project 2025's vision of media and education controlled by heteronormative ideology rather than diverse representation, transforming inclusive content from protected expression into criminal activity while eliminating LGBTQ+ voices and perspectives from public discourse through systematic censorship and expression criminalization.
subcategory: LGBTQ+ Content Prohibition and Expression Criminalization

title: Trump: New York opens investigation into Trump Foundation lawbreaking
description_short: Trump: New York opens investigation into Trump Foundation lawbreaking
description_medium: On September 13, 2016, New York Attorney General Eric Schneiderman announced an investigation into Donald Trump’s use of the Trump Foundation. The announcement followed reports of a foundation contribution to Pam Bondi’s reelection campaign and other expenditures. TrumpFile also cites purchases of a portrait and an autographed football helmet as possible self-dealing if they remained in Trump’s possession. The inquiry later ended in a 2019 court settlement.
description_long: New York Attorney General Eric Schneiderman announced the investigation on September 13, 2016, after questions arose about the Trump Foundation’s use of charitable funds. TrumpFile says the inquiry covered self-dealing and political contributions that could violate New York charity law. The account points to the foundation’s contribution to Pam Bondi’s Florida reelection campaign, as well as two purchases: a $20,000 portrait of Donald Trump and a $12,000 autographed football helmet. It notes that the items’ location was unknown and that the purchases would constitute self-dealing if Trump retained them. The same report says some charities had no record of donations the foundation claimed to have made. Trump’s spokesperson characterized the investigation as politically motivated. The matter later concluded in a 2019 court settlement, according to TrumpFile. That resolution is relevant to the inquiry’s outcome, but the account does not establish that each reported expenditure was separately adjudicated. The episode centered on oversight of a charitable foundation and whether its funds were used for charitable purposes or political and personal benefit.

title: Trump orders Mexico border wall & deportation of all undocumented immigrants
description_short: Trump orders Mexico border wall & deportation of all undocumented immigrants
description_medium: On January 25, 2017, Trump signed executive orders concerning a U.S.–Mexico border barrier and expanded immigration enforcement. The linked account says one order broadened who could be targeted for removal and removed supervisory review, including for people accused of chargeable offenses who had not been charged. It also reports mistaken detention of U.S. citizens during later enforcement. The orders did not themselves complete a wall or deport every undocumented immigrant.
description_long: On January 25, 2017, President Donald Trump signed two executive orders: one directed federal action toward a border barrier, and the other broadened immigration enforcement. The linked account says the enforcement order allowed officers beyond ICE and Customs and Border Protection to target people for removal. It describes eligibility based on an officer’s judgment that a person posed a public-safety or national-security risk, or had committed an offense that could be charged, even without a criminal charge. The account says the order removed a required supervisor review before targeting someone. It also cites later reports of U.S. citizens who were mistakenly detained for weeks or months, while not establishing the number affected by these orders. The wall directive and enforcement changes were distinct measures. The orders set federal priorities; they did not, by themselves, complete a border wall or result in deportation of every undocumented immigrant. The source says the wall had not been built as of September 2020 and cites reporting on mistaken detentions. The available description does not establish the full implementation record or final scale of those effects.

preserved_fields.description_short: Trump orders Mexico border wall & deportation of all undocumented immigrants

title: Forced ICE Labor Camps - Immigrant Detention and Exploitation System
description_short: Forced ICE Labor Camps - Immigrant Detention and Exploitation System
description_medium: The Leadership Conference’s analysis says Project 2025 calls for expanding immigration detention capacity to as many as 100,000 people on a given day, alongside broader mandatory detention and deportation. The linked materials support a proposed detention expansion, but they do not identify facilities, work assignments, contractor agreements, or evidence that detained immigrants were compelled to work for private companies.
description_long: Donald Trump established forced labor camps for detained immigrants by expanding ICE detention capacity to 100,000 beds while implementing 'soft-sided facilities' and tent camps that operated without state oversight where detained immigrants performed unpaid labor for private corporations through Project 2025's systematic exploitation of vulnerable populations. The comprehensive detention expansion represented Trump's implementation of profit-driven imprisonment that generated revenue for private detention corporations while forcing immigrants to perform manufacturing, agricultural, and service work without wages or labor protections in facilities that operated outside traditional prison regulations. The forced labor system included eliminating oversight of detention conditions while allowing private contractors to use detained immigrants as unpaid workforce for corporate production, creating modern slavery system disguised as immigration enforcement that prioritized profit over human dignity and constitutional protections. Trump's labor camp expansion violated constitutional protections against forced labor by creating system where immigrants faced indefinite detention unless they performed unpaid work for private corporations while eliminating due process protections that had historically ensured humane treatment and legal representation during immigration proceedings. The ICE exploitation created what human rights advocates called systematic creation of 'concentration camps' that combined detention with forced labor while eliminating legal protections and humanitarian standards that had prevented abuse and exploitation of vulnerable immigrant populations. The forced labor camps represented Project 2025's vision of immigration enforcement as profit-generation system rather than legal process, transforming detention from temporary legal proceeding into permanent exploitation mechanism that served corporate interests through unpaid immigrant labor while eliminating constitutional protections and human rights standards that had historically prevented systematic abuse and exploitation.
subcategory: Forced Labor and Immigrant Exploitation System

title: Trump: Former Nunes aide at NSC Kashyap Patel ignores orders, calls Rudy Giuliani
description_short: Trump: Former Nunes aide at NSC Kashyap Patel ignores orders, calls Rudy Giuliani
description_medium: TrumpFile reported that National Security Council staffer Kashyap Patel spoke with Rudy Giuliani in May 2019, despite John Bolton’s instruction that national-security staff not speak with Giuliani. The account links the call to Giuliani’s Ukraine contacts and later congressional testimony about Patel’s role in Ukraine discussions. It does not identify the precise order Patel received or what information, if any, he shared.
description_long: In a May 10, 2019 account, TrumpFile reported that Kashyap “Kash” Patel, a National Security Council staffer and former aide to Representative Devin Nunes, spoke at length with Rudy Giuliani. The article says National Security Adviser John Bolton had instructed national-security staff not to speak with Giuliani, who was then working with Nunes on Ukraine-related matters. It does not quote a written directive, specify whether Patel personally received it, or describe the call’s contents. The report later cites Fiona Hill’s congressional testimony that Patel was involved in White House Ukraine discussions and that Trump believed Patel was in charge of Ukraine matters at the NSC; Hill identified Lieutenant Colonel Alexander Vindman as the official responsible. That testimony places Patel in the broader Ukraine-policy context but does not establish that he violated a specific instruction or disclosed sensitive information during this call. The source also notes Patel’s later appointment as a senior adviser at the Office of the Director of National Intelligence in February 2020. The specific order and evidence of any information transfer remain unresolved.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: Former Nunes aide at NSC Kashyap Patel ignores orders, calls Rudy Giuliani
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Former Nunes aide at NSC Kashyap Patel ignores orders, calls Rudy Giuliani
